scope: Proposition 2.13 (Pure buffered RSW consequences) of the manuscript “SLE3 universality for weak finite-range Ising interactions” (preprints/SLE3-universality-for-weak-finite-range-Ising-interactions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 44a7837e35328259), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 15. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a finite collection of polygonal corridors, each a topological rectangle with designated opposite end gates, and polygonal annular bands. Prescribe one color for each required crossing or circuit. Assume each requirement admits a finite rectangle construction with positive-width unpinned buffers, and that the buffered constructions for opposite colors are disjoint. Their simultaneous occurrence has probability bounded below by a positive constant for all sufficiently fine meshes. The constant may depend on this fixed geometry, and is uniform over pins beyond the buffers and ambient plane or torus laws with common lattice charts. There are C < ∞, ρ > 0 such that, in a buffered bulk annulus and for 1 ≤ r < R/C, P(a monochromatic spin arm or a resolved contour passage from Br to Bc R) ≤ C(r/R)ρ . (2.9) For the monochromatic event either color may be specified or both allowed. The annular construction may be conditioned on earlier reveals that remain outside its unpinned test collars. Fixed-factor changes of radii and bounded lattice drawing corrections change only the constants.
